title.narrative: South Sudan Reconciliation, Stabilization, and Resilience Trust Fund (RSRTF)
South Sudan Reconciliation, Stabilization, and Resilience Trust Fund (RSRTF)

description.narrative:
Huvudsyftet med RSRTF är att stödja mer resiliensinriktad programmering genom att rikta stödet till utvalda områden där förutsättningarna för att främja de miljöer som är nödvändiga för att möjliggöra det långsiktiga engagemang som krävs för att uppnå långsiktiga utvecklingsmål. Insatsen syftar till ökad finansiering och ökat engagemang i politiska, freds- och säkerhetsfrågor där finansieringen har begränsats, liksom att överbrygga fredsbevarande och säkerhets-, humanitära och utvecklingsinsatser.
Fondens mål är 1) Stödåtgärder som bidrar till säkrare miljöer 2) Uppmuntra strategisk och gemensam programmering för att överbrygga fredsbevarande och säkerhets- och utvecklingsinsatser och 3) Främja hållbara, lokalt ledda, kontextspecifika och oevidensbaseradeinitiativ på lokal nivå.
Fonden kommer att stödja strategiska insatser som analyserar konfliktdynamiken ur ett holistiskt perspektiv och som fokuserar på lokalt anpassade lösningar för att ta itu med eller minska orsakerna till politiska, säkerhets-, sociala eller ekonomiska sårbarheter. Fonden kommer att anta en områdesbaserad programmeringsmetod som riktar sig till specifika områden där möjligheter finns att leverera förändring och bryta sig ur konflikter, våld och givarberoende. Fonden kommer att spela en effektiv roll när det gäller att främja starkare lokalt fokus på hur resurserna fördelas och säkerställa lokalt förankrad analys som återspeglar områdets unika karaktär och lokala konfliktaktörer. För varje strategiskt område som identifieras av fonden så kommer en områdesreferensgrupp (ARG) att sammankallas för att genomföra en detaljerad analys av lokala konflikter, samt lokal politisk- och säkerhetsdynamik. ARG kommer att identifiera befintliga resurser, inklusive erfarenheter och reflektioner såsom lokala traditioner, praxis och kapacitet för fred. Tillsammans kommer ARG att identifiera kollektiva projektinterventioner som tar itu med viktiga drivkrafter för instabilitet och samhällsupplösning och stödjande samhällen för att uppnå de långsiktiga vinsterna av bestående fred.

The main objective of the RSRTF is to support the drive towards more resilience focused programming by fostering stable political and security environments necessary to enable the sustained engagements required to achieve long-term recovery and development goals. This trough providing funding for increased engagement on political, peace and security issues where the funding has been limited as well as by bridging peacekeeping and security, humanitarian, and long-term recovery and development efforts.
The objectives of the fund include 1) Support actions that contribute to stable political and security environments; 2) Encourage strategic and joint programming to bridge peacekeeping and security, recovery and development efforts; and 3) Promote sustainable locally-led, context specific and evidence-based action.
The Fund will support strategic interventions that appraise conflict dynamics holistically and apply appropriate solutions to address or diminish root causes whether political, security, social, or economic. The Fund will adopt an area-based programming approach, targeting distinct locations where opportunities exist to deliver transformational change and move beyond cycles of conflict, violence and aid dependency. The Fund will play an effective role in promoting stronger local focus in the way resources are programmed and ensure locally led analysis reflective of the unique nature of the area and the local drivers of conflict. For each strategic area identified by the Fund Steering Committee, an Area Reference Group will be convened to conduct detailed analysis of localized conflict, political and security dynamics. The ARG will identify existing resources, including lessons and reflections on indigenous traditions, practices and capacities for peace. Together the ARG will identify collective project interventions that tackle key drivers of instability and societal disintegration and support communities to realize the long-term gains of sustained peace.

The South Sudan Reconciliation, Stabilization and Resilience Trust Fund (RSRTF) is a multi-donor, inter-agency pooled fund established in 2019 and supported by seven donors and implemented by the UN family, in partnership with national and international non-governmental organisations.
It promotes integrated area-based programming (ABP) built around three essential elements: 1. Reconciliation: Rebuild trust and confidence, strengthen social cohesion, and promote peaceful coexistence through gender and age-sensitive communal conflict prevention, management and resolution. 2. Stabilization: Broaden participation in and enhance space for peaceful political processes, strengthen the social contract between citizens and the state, and support restoration of security, the rule of law and access to justice. 3. Resilience: Invest in capacities, assets and opportunities that foster inter-dependency between communities, deter the mobilization of at-risk youth and promote social integration, equality, agency and self-reliance to realize peace dividends that shift incentives and raise the cost of resorting to violence.
It is operating in distinct geographic locations - hot spots - where opportunities exist to deliver transformational change and move beyond cycles of conflict and violence. While focusing on conflict resolution and peace-building at the community level, the ABPs take a holistic approach, the objectives of the fund are: 1) Support actions that contribute to stable political and security environments; 2) Encourage strategic and joint programming to bridge peacekeeping and security, recovery and development efforts; and 3) Promote sustainable locally-led, context specific and evidence-based action.
The RSRTF aims to build conditions of peace and stability conducive for enabling viable resilience endeavors. The fund aims to improve efforts across development, humanitarian and peace-building spectra, providing strategic financing to specific areas, to lessen the destructive drivers of conflict and develop more peaceful and, ultimately, self-reliant communities.

description.narrative:
Since the beginning of the Trust Fund in 2019, it has mobilized 100MUSD from seven donors (Canada, European Union, Japan, The Netherlands, Norway, Sida, Switzerland) allocated to five area-based programs (ABPs) and three small projects under the thematic grants window. Some examples of the results include: - 79 conflict management and reconciliation interventions carried out to de-escalate and address tensions over abductions, cattle restitution, blood compensation and other critical issues involving shuttle diplomacy and mediation dialogues; - 104 community-based protection and dispute resolution mechanisms established and supported - Training of 1,310 (535 male, 775 female) faith-based leaders, primary school teachers, workers, local chiefs and community mobilizers, youths and women carried out, focusing on grassroot conflict mediation, prevention of abductions and SGBV, positive masculinity and women leadership - 78 abducted persons (22 women, 56 children) released and reunited with their families 2032 children supported to return to and stay in formal primary and secondary education
In terms of the specific area-based programs, the following can be noted: 1) Koch county areabased program II (12/2021 11/2023) This areabased program (ABP), now in its second phase, has contributed to consolidate and expand stabilization gains, allowing partners to invest time and effort to develop and strengthen the structures and behaviors needed to nurture longterm transformational change. Between July and December 2022, Koch and its neighboring counties witnessed a reduction in cattle raids and intercommunal violence, and reported an upsurge in trading activities between counties, as well as an increasing number of people moving from the Bentiu camp for internally displaced people to resettle in areas covered by the ABP. The peace conferences organised at state level, the peace dialogue between Koch, Mayendit and Leer counties, as well as the series of communitylevel peace dialogues and awareness raising have contributed to create enabling conditions from the internally displaced people to return to their villages.
2.Warrap/Western Bahr el Ghazal/Warrap ABP (01/2020-04/2022). This area-based program, which ended on 30 April 2022, contributed through a whole-of-system approach with reconciliation, stabilization and resilience components, to visible reduction of violence related to cattle migration.
The interventions contributed to strengthen capacity at the community level of peace committees, local chiefs and youth to enhance conflict management and peace-building. It also contributed to decrease competition and conflict over major perennial water sources and reduce livestock movement into neighboring farmers and other pastoralist community areas through rehabilitation and construction of water infrastructure along approved migration routes. Three boreholes were constructed, nine community-based pasture management groups (six for common grazing land and three pasture management committees) were established. Sustainable water and pasture management practices were adopted, like rotational grazing, fencing off water points and controlling the number of animals using water points at any one time by allowing them access in shifts. The ABP also contributed to the rehabilitation of a 48-kilometre road linking Western Bahr el Ghazal and Warrap states (Kuajena and Pagol payams), facilitating access to markets and deepening social cohesion.
3. Jonglei/Greater Pibor Administrative Area (GPAA) areabased program (01/202003/2023) Since the start of this areabased program (ABP), now in its second phase, redution of violence is seen in Jonglei and Greater Pibor Administrative Area (GPAA). Efforts made by peacebuilding partners to deescalate tensions and reduce mobilization of armed youth have resulted in meaningful improvements to community perceptions of safety and security across all target areas. More than 1,200 youth and women (606 women and 594 men) have engaged in resiliencebuilding activities, learnt crop farming cultivation and vegetable gardening, community access roads have been constructed and 26 kilometres of drainage channel restored in Akobo West and Pibor. Rehabilitations of community access roads and the landing strip have enabled safe and secure movement of community members while they carry out their livelihood activities. In the face of flooding, 21 kilometres of road dykes have protected homes and livelihoods. This allowed air flights to land and deliver commodities, and community members have been able to produce food crops and vegetables locally to supplement their dietary and nutrition needs. Despite a temporary setbeck in December 2022, when armed youth from Akobo, Duk, Nyirol and Uror attacked people in Gumuruk and Nanaam, there has been a noticeable increase in social cohesion and peaceful coexistence throughout the area
4. Central Equatoria areabased program (10/2021 - 09/2023) In 2022, there was a noticeable reduction of insecurity in southern Central Equatoria region, reported against indicators such as the return of communities, general stability that has led to increase of mobility, some resurgence of economic activities and the productive engagement of youth. The peace-building activities of this area-based program (ABP) have focused on improving relations between politically divided communities as well as between returnees and host communities, as well as between returnees and host communities, bringing people together to discuss peaceful coexistence and conflict resolution using dialogue rather than violence. Civil-military dialogue meetings were held, aiming at strengthening trust among he different actors, namely law enforcement actors (police, army) and communities, and reducing tensions while promoting peace. The ABP peace-building activities have, where possible, engaged highlevel decision-makers and community leaders, as well as women, youth and elderly people.
5. 'Kong Koc' Greater Tonj/Warrap areabased program (8/2022 - 8/2024) Launched in August 2022, the 'Kong Koc' ABP is the fifth and newest areabased program (ABP), designed to tackle the multilayered and complex dynamics that underpin ongoing violence in Tonj. 'Kong Koc', meaning to wait', illustrates the communities in Greater Tonj waiting for peace and development after years of intercommunal violence. By the end of December 2022, the preparations were completed and the project could fully start. The project has so far contributed to create an enabling environment expected to contribute to improving peace and conflict dynamics in target communities. The inception meetings, held in Tonj, Warrap and Paliang, were attended by a various levels of formal and informal authorities at all administrative levels (county, payam and boma), chiefs, cattle camp leaders and women representatives, with the aim of introducing the project and raising awareness around planned intervention. 12 peace monitoring committees were formed and trained at payam level (105 male, 84 female), three county monitoring committees (51 men, 20 women) and three reference groups at county level (26 men, 19 women). The committees include representatives of women, cattle camp leaders, chiefs, sub-chiefs and non-governmental organizations as well as members of the prison service, police service, local government and other peace partners operating in the area. Some activities started, such as training of peace monitoring committees to empower participants on early warning of conflict and conflict management, as well as on roles and responsibilities of peace monitoring committees in the community. UNMISS peacekeepers started patrolling conflict hotspots to curtail tensions between communities, deter violence and build confidence.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
